So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?}

{76–77} {Reclining on green cushions}; that is, the companions of these two gardens recline on green cushions, which are the carpets beneath the elevated seats, which have been increased beyond their seats, so that there is a rippling behind their seats, for increased splendor and beauty of appearance. {And beautiful rich carpets}: al-'Abqari is attributed to everything woven finely and excellently, and for this reason He described them with beauty that encompasses the beauty of quality, [the beauty of] appearance, and softness of touch.

These two gardens are below the first two, as Allah explicitly stated by His saying: {And besides them are two other gardens}. As He described the first two with a number of attributes that He did not ascribe to the latter two: He said of the first two, {in them are two flowing springs}, and of the latter two, {two gushing springs}; the difference between a flowing and a gushing spring is well known. He said of the first two, {having branches}, and did not say this of the latter two. He said of the first two, {in them is of every fruit two kinds}, and of the latter two, {in them is fruit, date palms, and pomegranates}; the difference between these two descriptions is known. He said of the first two, describing their wives and spouses, {in them are those who restrain their glances [no man or jinn has touched them before them]}, and of the latter two, {maidens sheltered in pavilions}; the difference between these is evident. He said of the first two, {Is the reward of good anything but good?}, which indicates that the first two are the reward of the good-doers, and He did not say this of the latter two. The mere mention of the first two before the latter two also indicates their superiority.

By these aspects the superiority of the first two over the latter two is known, and that the first two are prepared for those brought near, from among the prophets, the truthful, and the chosen righteous servants of Allah, while the latter two are prepared for the general believers. In each of the mentioned gardens is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived; in them is what souls desire and eyes delight in. Their people are in the utmost ease, contentment, tranquility, and goodly abode, to the extent that each of them sees no one in a better state than himself, nor anyone with a higher bliss than the one he is in.

{78} When He mentioned the vastness of His bounty and His kindness, He said: {Blessed is the name of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor}; that is, exalted and abundant is His goodness, to whom belong overwhelming majesty, perfect glory, and honor for His friends.

The commentary on Surah ar-Rahman is complete. And to Allah belong all praise, thanks, and good commendation.

{46–47} That is: and for the one who feared his Lord and stood in awe before Him, so he abandoned what He forbade and did what He commanded, there are {two gardens}, of gold, their vessels, adornments, structures, and all that is in them. The first of the two gardens is a reward for abandoning what is forbidden, and the other is a reward for performing acts of obedience.

{48–49} Among the attributes of these two gardens is that they are {having branches}; that is, in them are the various kinds of bounty, the bounty of the outward and the inward, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. That is, in them are abundant flourishing trees with soft branches, upon which are abundant, luscious, and delicious ripe fruits.

{50–51} And in those two gardens are {two flowing springs}, which they cause to gush forth as they wish and desire.

{52–53} {In them is of every fruit} of all kinds of fruits {two kinds}; that is, two varieties, each variety having a flavor and color that the other kind does not have.

{54–55} {Reclining on couches whose linings are of brocade}: this describes the couches of the people of Paradise and their sitting upon them, and that they recline upon them; that is, sitting with settled composure, ease, and comfort, like the sitting of kings on thrones. The description and beauty of those couches is known only to Allah, the Exalted. Even their linings, which are next to the ground, are of brocade (istabraq), which is the finest and most precious silk; so how much more so are their outer surfaces, which they touch. {And the fruit of the two gardens is near at hand}: al-Jana is the fruit that is ripe and easily reached; that is, the fruit of these two gardens is within easy reach, attainable by one standing, sitting, or lying down.

Rather, they are virgins, loving and beloved by their husbands through their goodly conduct, coquetry, charm, and grace. For this reason He said: {as if they were rubies and coral}, because of their purity, the beauty of their appearance, and their radiance.

These two lofty gardens are for those brought near.
